records.people: National Bank of Moldova management and Executive Committee (unnamed); Supervisory Board
records.summary: The Court of Accounts of the Republic of Moldova, by Decision no. 62 of 5 November 2019, published in the Monitorul Oficial on 29 November 2019, reported on a compliance audit of the National Bank of Moldova's administrative expenditure budgets and investment allocations for 2015 to 2018. It found non-compliance by responsible persons with certain provisions, performance bonuses paid without any regulation of incentive conditions, assets placed in inappropriate depreciation categories creating uncertainty over 4.1 million lei of book value, and concert organisation services worth 0.87 million lei procured with deficiencies relative to the regulatory framework with a possible impact on public revenues. This record rests on a specialist accounting-news report of the decision rather than on the Court's own published text, which could not be retrieved here.
records.detail: This is a separate episode from the 2012-2016 banking-fraud investigation already on the map: different years, a different subject matter (the bank's own administrative spending and procurement), a different investigating body (the supreme audit institution rather than prosecutors), and no named individuals. The audit was reported as concluding that expenditure was executed in line with the regulatory framework in all material respects while identifying the uncertain situations listed above. The report was directed to the National Bank of Moldova, the Ministry of Finance, the Government and Parliament.
records.source_title: Curtea de Conturi: auditul devizelor de cheltuieli si a alocatiilor pentru investitii ale BNM
records.refused_reason: REFUSED at round 71. The Court of Accounts did audit the National Bank of Moldova (Decision no. 62 of 5 November 2019, administrative expense budgets and investment allocations 2015-2018), but its conclusion is that the audited expenses were executed 'in all significant respects, in accordance with the regulatory framework' -- a clean opinion. Its findings are mostly that the RULES lack specifics: performance bonuses granted 'in the absence of exhaustive rules on how the amount is determined', depreciation-category uncertainty on 4.1m lei of book value, and unclear compliance on connecting flights because the national framework is silent. The one adverse item is 0.87m lei of concert-organisation services procured with deficiencies. Filing a corruption case on a compliance-positive audit would colour Moldova for a document that cleared it. Kept as a documented negative instead: an SAI examined this bank and found compliance. It becomes a record if a later Court of Accounts decision makes an adverse finding.

records.kind: central bank law put under government-ordered review
records.summary: Terms of reference published by the Australian Treasury on 20 July 2022 put the Reserve Bank of Australia's own statutory objectives under external review, directing the reviewers to assess the RBA's objectives as set out in the Reserve Bank Act 1959, including the continued appropriateness of the inflation targeting framework, the bank's governance including board structure, composition, expertise and the appointments process, its accountability arrangements, and its culture, management and recruitment processes, with a final report of recommendations to go to the Treasurer by March 2023. Distinct from the July 2023 public pressure episode already on the map.
records.source_title: Australian Treasury, 'Reserve Bank of Australia review - Terms of reference', 20 July 2022
records.refused_reason: REFUSED at round 71 on round 70's Bundesbank rule: this row records the state moving AGAINST the bank, and the bank welcomed this review, so there is no adversary. RBA governor Philip Lowe said of the terms of reference 'The terms of reference are appropriate and the Government has appointed a first-class panel', and the Treasurer said he had 'worked closely with the bank' to settle them and that it was 'not about taking shots. It's not about pointing blame.' Australia keeps its July 2023 public-pressure record. This reverses only on a source showing the RBA opposed the review or its terms.

records.people: Claire M. C. Kennedy (member of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Canada, December 2012 - November 2025; Lead Director July 2018 - July 2025)
records.move: sat on the Bank of Canada's Board of Directors for thirteen years, as Lead Director from 2018, while a senior tax partner and then Senior Advisor at the law firm Bennett Jones LLP, and while a director of Alamos Gold Inc., Constellation Software Inc. and CDL Global and chair of Neo Performance Materials Inc.
records.summary: The Bank of Canada's own profile page for Kennedy states she was appointed to its Board of Directors from December 2012 to November 2025, served as the Board's Lead Director from July 2018 to July 2025, and over the same period 'served as a senior tax partner at Bennett Jones LLP before becoming Senior Advisor, Clients and Industries', retiring from the firm in June 2025, alongside directorships at Alamos Gold, Constellation Software and CDL Global. The private side is the law partnership in which she was herself a partner, i.e. an owner-member, and the four named companies, none of them a state body; this is a concurrent private-sector role held while on the central bank's board, filed on the same footing as the map's existing Taiwan board record.
records.source_title: Claire M. C. Kennedy - Bank of Canada, Board of Directors profile
records.quote: served as a senior tax partner at Bennett Jones LLP before becoming Senior Advisor, Clients and Industries
records.refused_reason: REFUSED at round 71 on the settled rule that private but not FINANCIAL is logged, not filed. Every concurrent role the Bank of Canada's own profile names is outside finance: senior tax partner and then Senior Advisor at the law firm Bennett Jones LLP, and directorships at Alamos Gold (mining), Constellation Software, CDL Global and the chair of Neo Performance Materials. That is the Slovakia, Teeters, Lindsey and Brimmer line, and the shape round 54 nearly filed for Seychelles, which would have counted a farming and manufacturing career as a move through private finance. The concurrent-seat shape itself is fine -- the map carries Taiwan's SinoPac record on it -- so this reverses on a concurrent role at a financial firm. Canada keeps its Carney/Goldman Sachs record.
